title: Bridging the Gap between Unstructured SpMM and Structured Sparse Tensor Cores
problem: Sparse-dense Matrix Multiplication (SpMM) on Tensor Cores is inefficient for unstructured sparse matrices due to low block-wise density, causing computational waste. Specialized Sparse Tensor Cores (SpTCs) require strict 2:4 or 1:2 structured sparsity, creating a mismatch with real-world unstructured sparse data.
motivation: SpMM is critical for AI/ML and scientific computing workloads. While Tensor Cores provide speedup for dense operations, unstructured sparsity (common in neural networks and simulations) cannot leverage SpTC acceleration directly. This gap leaves significant performance on the table.
method: MP-SpMM: A Matching and Padding approach inspired by graph theory's maximum matching problem to transform unstructured sparse matrices into structured sparsity patterns compatible with SpTCs. Includes novel storage format and highly optimized GPU kernel.
key_novelty: Graph-theory-inspired matching algorithm that converts arbitrary sparse patterns to SpTC-compatible structured sparsity without excessive padding; optimized GPU kernel exploiting SpTC capabilities for unstructured inputs.
contributions: MP-SpMM algorithm bridging unstructured and structured sparsity via maximum matching
Novel storage format for transformed sparse matrices
Highly optimized GPU kernel for SpTC execution
hardware_target: NVIDIA GPUs with Sparse Tensor Cores
limitations: Requires structured sparsity pattern conversion; performance depends on matching quality; may have overhead for sparse patterns with poor matchability.
